title: The affordance surface offers release.decide per goal, so the Release card has something to spend
description:
PRODUCER ROW filed by architect-aa54e231 on 2026-09-06 while planning task-817d893fa1254a4d82d2888af1f87a47 (the Gate 3 browser proof), which now declares dependsOn against this row. Global rail 20 (spun-out rows) and global rail 4 clause 2 (a proof row's missing capability becomes a prerequisite production row with the gap measured symbol by symbol, never a mock-backed journey).

THE GAP: `release.decide` IS SERVED BUT IS OFFERED NOWHERE. Measured at HEAD on moe/work-2026-09-04, three ways:

(1) IT IS SERVED. `daemon-command-async-entries.ts:332-335` registers it as an async entry with `payloadKeys: PAYLOAD_KEYS[RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND]` and `requiredCapability: CAPABILITIES.GOAL`, and :170 fences it through `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS`. `git grep -n "release\.decide" -- apps packages adapters` minus tests returns 17 production hits across the contract, the service, the vocabulary, the payload keys, the spawn fence and the generated client. The kind is fully landed by task-f961dc89 and task-bda0eeac.

(2) IT IS NOT OFFERED. `git grep -n "release\.decide\|RELEASE_DECIDE" -- apps/daemon/src/http` minus tests returns ZERO. It is not a bootstrap kind either (`grep -n release apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-contracts.ts` returns nothing), so it does not get the generic emission at affordance-read.ts:282-284 that `deployment.set_target` gets.

(3) THE LADDER'S OFFER UNION IS A CLOSED TYPE THAT EXCLUDES IT. `affordance-planning-offers.ts:146-147` types the mintable kinds as exactly `"approval.decide" | "approval.decide_intent" | "goal.close" | "plan.propose" | "preview.decide" | "repository.publish"`. Adding a seventh is a type edit, not just a new call.

WHY THIS BLOCKS THE PROOF ROW. The Release card follows the PUBLISH card, which finds its offer in the frame: `goal-publish.tsx:39-41` matches `row["commandKind"] === "repository.publish" && row["targetAggregateId"] === `publish:${goalId}``, and :86 says "Nothing landed means no offer and no receipt: the card is not a thing on this screen at all". `spendOffer` (offer-wire.ts:62-69) takes the offer row as its `affordance` argument. With no offer minted, the Release card can never render and `spendOffer` has nothing to spend — so task-817d893f's DoD 2, 5 and 6 are unsatisfiable, and its DoD 3 ("absent when unoffered") would be vacuously and permanently true.

THE PRECEDENT TO FOLLOW IS TWO LINES AWAY. `preview.decide` is minted at affordance-planning-offers.ts:222-224 as `input.previewReceipt(goal.goalId) === "STARTED" ? [offer(input, "preview.decide", previewAggregateId(goal.goalId))] : []`, and `repository.publish` at :210 as `input.landedCommit(goal.goalId) ? [offer(input, "repository.publish", `publish:${goal.goalId}`)] : []`. Both take a LAZY FACT on `PlanningOfferInput` supplied by the composition root in affordance-read.ts, exactly as `closeReadiness` and `landedCommit` do.

THE TARGET KEY MUST NOT BE THE BARE GOAL ID, and this is a SAFETY property with a comment already written at :216-220 explaining why for preview: `readDurableLedger` keeps the last committed result per `targetAggregateId`, so a decide targeted at the goal itself OVERWRITES THE GOAL'S STATE and drops it from `durableGoals` entirely. The release offer inherits that hazard exactly. Use a distinct key (`release:<goalId>` follows `publish:<goalId>`) and say so at the site.

THE WITHHOLDING DECISION THIS ROW MUST MAKE, and it has two defensible horns - decide it deliberately and write it at the offer site: (a) WITHHOLD until the evidence is complete, following `goal.close`, whose comment at :225-231 says "the surface must never offer a close the command would refuse"; or (b) OFFER whenever the goal is releasable in principle and let the dispatch refuse RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE, so the operator SEES why. Note the tension before choosing: task-817d893f's DoD 2 requires the operator to see `RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE` verbatim with its missing criterion ids, which horn (a) would make unreachable from the browser. Whichever you choose, the consumer's DoD depends on it, so state it in a comment and assert it.

NOT IN SCOPE: the Release card and its journey (task-817d893f owns them), the release dossier (task-70a7ccd3, DONE), the kind and its service (task-f961dc89, DONE).
definitionOfDone: The affordance read offers `release.decide` for a goal, targeted at a key that is NOT the bare goal id - asserted BY VALUE on `targetAggregateId` against the PRODUCTION surface read, never a hand-built frame. `git grep -n "release\.decide" -- apps/daemon/src/http` minus tests currently returns ZERO; that must become nonzero through a real mint site.

THE TARGET KEY IS DISTINCT FROM THE GOAL AGGREGATE, and a test proves the goal survives a release decision: commit a decide, then assert the goal is STILL present in the durable goal set and its own state is unchanged. affordance-planning-offers.ts:216-220 records why - `readDurableLedger` keeps the last committed result per targetAggregateId, so a goal-targeted decide silently erases the goal. Assert the survival, not merely the key's spelling.

THE WITHHOLDING RULE IS DECIDED, WRITTEN AT THE OFFER SITE AND ASSERTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS as an offered-kind SET, not a subset: a `not.toContain` alone passes if the surface emitted a differently-named release offer. State which horn you took (withhold until evidence is complete, following goal.close; or offer and let the dispatch refuse RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE so the operator sees it) and why, naming the consumer clause it serves.

The fact the ladder reads is a LAZY FACT on `PlanningOfferInput` supplied by the composition root, following `closeReadiness`, `landedCommit` and `previewReceipt` - not a store handle reached from inside the ladder, and resolved only for a goal that could actually be offered a release. A per-poll walk over every goal is the 09-05 affordances hot-path incident repeating.

Every asserting consumer of the offered-kind set is censused WHOLE-TREE and named with a verdict - `git grep -ln "affordance|nextAllowed|offered" -- 'tests/**'` plus the affordance test files under apps/daemon/src/http. Any test pinning an offered SET by exact membership or a COUNT reds when a seventh kind appears; find those before the gate does and say which needed an arm and why the others did not.

MUTATION DRILL, quoted with its failing line: target the offer at the bare goal id and confirm BOTH the by-value arm AND the goal-survival arm go RED. Restore per global rail 13 - back the path up out of tree, restore from the backup rather than `git checkout --`, prove by sha256 in a call separate from the restore.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line; if the census found consumers under tests/**, say which lanes you ran and which you did not.
taskRails: THE OFFER IS THE MISSING PIECE, NOT THE CARD. The kind is landed and served (async entry at daemon-command-async-entries.ts:332-335); only the mint is absent. Do NOT build the Release card or its journey - task-817d893f owns those and declares dependsOn on this row.

FOLLOW THE preview.decide AND repository.publish PRECEDENT at affordance-planning-offers.ts:210 and :222-224 - a lazy fact on PlanningOfferInput, supplied by the composition root in affordance-read.ts. A second pattern for the same problem is a second thing to reason about.

THE TARGET KEY IS A SAFETY PROPERTY, NOT TIDINESS. A decide targeted at the bare goal id overwrites the goal's last committed result and drops it from `durableGoals` - the comment at :216-220 already states this for preview. Prove the goal survives.
THE OFFER UNION AT :146-147 IS A CLOSED TYPE. Adding the kind is a type edit plus a mint site; a mint without the type widening will not compile, and a widening without a mint offers nothing.
DECIDE THE WITHHOLDING RULE DELIBERATELY AND WRITE IT DOWN. The consumer's DoD depends on which horn you take, and an undocumented choice reads as an accident to the row that consumes it.
